scope: The visual round of the message surface: roomier cards, a translucent surface, an exit animation, a dismissal that takes two steps, a visual page that behaves like the product, and the css minifier the modern features need. Plus one layering fix the full end to end run found, and three defects the delta review of that round found: the focus after a message goes away, the same on a platform that does not focus a button when it is clicked, and a leaving message that still took clicks. No push, no merge, no tag move, no dependency or lockfile change.

checks.engineFloor: Chrome 123 / Safari 17.5 / Firefox 120, declared in build.cssTarget. The floor is the lowest version of the one feature the design depends on (light-dark, which carries the theme); color-mix, :has, text-wrap, @starting-style and scrollbar-gutter are progressive and do not raise it. Below the floor is out of scope and the module carries no fallback. The minifier is esbuild, because the css target only says which version to lower to and Lightning CSS lowered light-dark() anyway; the built css was checked for the leftovers of that rewrite and has none, and light-dark() and color-mix() are both in it as written.

defectsFoundDuringReview.symptom: in the application the cards had no border, no padding and square buttons
defectsFoundDuringReview.cause: Tailwind drops any layer order statement the application writes, so the message layer was registered first and became the lowest one; the preflight won
defectsFoundDuringReview.fix: the stylesheet is imported into Tailwind's components layer, so it sits above the preflight and below the utilities; the component entry no longer imports it, two owners produced two copies and the first copy decided the layer
defectsFoundDuringReview.guard: tests/e2e/message-presentation.spec.ts measures the card in the application, where the preflight is present; it fails when the import moves back

defectsFoundDuringReview.symptom: closing a message dropped the focus back to the body
defectsFoundDuringReview.cause: the focused close button is removed with the message
defectsFoundDuringReview.fix: the list remembers the region while the button is attached and moves the focus to the next control, or to the programmatically focusable region

defectsFoundDuringReview.symptom: the module was light in the dark application: its border, background and padding were gone
defectsFoundDuringReview.cause: Lightning CSS rewrote light-dark() inside a custom property as var(--lightningcss-light,X)var(--lightningcss-dark,Y); those variables are never defined, so the value was invalid; the dev server does not rewrite it, so the standalone sample looked right
defectsFoundDuringReview.fix: the minifier is esbuild, because the css target only names the version to lower to and the lowering still happened; the module carries no fallback for older engines
defectsFoundDuringReview.guard: the end to end test measures the real background colour of a card in the application, in the dark theme; the built css was also checked for the leftovers of the rewrite

defectsFoundDuringReview.id: the assertion named a colour that never existed
defectsFoundDuringReview.symptom: the background assertion expected a colour that no version of the module ever had
defectsFoundDuringReview.cause: the stylesheet was changed without running that assertion, so the value drifted and nothing said so
defectsFoundDuringReview.fix: the assertion pins the dark branch exactly and requires an alpha below 1, so the transparency can be tuned without touching it
defectsFoundDuringReview.guard: tests/e2e/message-presentation.spec.ts measures the real background colour of a card in the application

defectsFoundDuringReview.symptom: the export window's confirm button could not be clicked while an import result was on screen; the resource bundle export failed
defectsFoundDuringReview.cause: the region sat above the dialogs (60 against 50); the region was narrow enough to miss them until the card grew, and then the import result landed on the button
defectsFoundDuringReview.fix: the region now sits below the dialogs and above the top bar, which is where the application keeps its overlays; the dialog is modal and owns the screen
defectsFoundDuringReview.guard: tests/e2e/message-region.spec.ts checks the point of the confirm button; the layer was put back the way it was and the test does fail that way

defectsFoundDuringReview.id: the focus was lost when a message timed out
defectsFoundDuringReview.symptom: a keyboard user who tabbed into a message and left it alone lost their place when it timed out after ten seconds
defectsFoundDuringReview.cause: the timer called the store directly, so the list never learned the message was going away and never moved the focus; the button that had the focus was removed with it
defectsFoundDuringReview.fix: the timer goes through the same dismiss path as the close button; the callback it depends on is stable, so the timer is not reset whenever a notice arrives
defectsFoundDuringReview.guard: tests/e2e/message-region.spec.ts waits for the ten seconds and asks where the focus is now

defectsFoundDuringReview.id: the focus was lost when a message was closed on a platform that does not focus buttons
defectsFoundDuringReview.symptom: closing a message dropped the focus to the body on macOS, where a click does not focus a button
defectsFoundDuringReview.cause: the region was derived from the focused element, and on that platform the focused element is still the body after a click, so there was no region to hand the focus back to
defectsFoundDuringReview.fix: the region is the element the workbench already owns, so it is handed down instead of being guessed from the focus
defectsFoundDuringReview.guard: tests/e2e/message-region.spec.ts clicks the button programmatically, which moves no focus, and is what a click on macOS looks like to the page; it fails when the fix is taken out

defectsFoundDuringReview.id: a leaving message still took clicks
defectsFoundDuringReview.symptom: an invisible message held the clicks in that corner of the screen for the two hundred milliseconds its exit takes
defectsFoundDuringReview.cause: the leaving rule set the opacity and the offset but not the pointer events
defectsFoundDuringReview.fix: the leaving rule also turns the pointer events off
defectsFoundDuringReview.guard: tests/e2e/message-region.spec.ts reads the computed pointer events of the card while it is leaving

openItems.id: the card has no real blur
openItems.detail: the surface is translucent at 0.94 and the bleed-through stopped, but there is no backdrop blur under it. The earlier reason for leaving it out no longer holds: with esbuild and the explicit css target the built css keeps the standard backdrop-filter (Tailwind's own backdrop utilities are emitted with both forms, checked in the built file). So this is a design question now, not a toolchain one: whether to blur, how much, and how that pairs with the alpha.

openItems.id: when the save failure notice goes away
openItems.detail: it now waits for the user to acknowledge it. Whether a later successful save takes it away by itself is not defined in the design.
